ahr19430817-01.2.31.note: three in one column: the body of an unidentified Arab beggar found in the east of the town, transferred to the Government Hospital; Hasan Ahmad Shahada struck by an army car near Acre; and Hasna Hasan Hamdan, aged 8, hit by a lorry in Hijaz Street, who "died of her injuries on the way to the Government Hospital."

ahr19430903-01.2.53.note: Abd al-Latif Rashid shot in the neck in an alley of the Arab market; "transferred in a critical condition to the Government Hospital and consciousness has not yet returned to him."

ahr19440406-01.2.69.note: Alexander Goldberger killed in a work accident at the Haifa refineries; body to the Government Hospital.

ahr19440606-01.2.75.note: an English constable in plain clothes stabbed three deep knife-wounds at the end of Shomer Street; "the stabber spoke Arabic"; he reached the police station and was gathered from there to the Government Hospital.

ahr19440627-01.2.62.note: Yafa Cohen, 28, of 14 Gilad Street, found lifeless in her flat; the body transferred for examination to the Government Hospital; a suicide by strychnine is supposed.

ahr19440920-01.2.53.note: four more brought in recent days, 2 died; deaths so far 9 Arabs, 1 Jew, 1 Englishman

ahr19441003-01.2.53.note: a further Arab case, admitted to "the infectious-diseases department of the Government Hospital"

ahr19450105-01.2.93.note: after a long interval two more Arabs; 72 cases in all, 22 dead, 47 recovered, 3 in hospital

ahr19450812-01.2.61.note: Pinhas Sirkin of Tel Hai Street, Haifa, run over and killed by an army car as he stepped off a public bus bound for Nahariya; body gathered to the Government Hospital.

ahr19451102-01.2.71.note: an explosion at the refineries in Haifa Bay; a crushed body recovered from the debris, identified from his papers as Yaakov Goldberg (or Grinberg); gathered to the Government Hospital.

ahr19451202-01.2.48.note: a car carrying Arab Legion soldiers collides with a locomotive inside the port; four injured soldiers gathered to the Government Hospital; the Jewish driver, also injured, held for questioning.

ahr19460910-01.2.8.note: a British CID sergeant shot by the Windsor Hotel, hit in seven places, "gathered to the Government Hospital and there died"; Sergeant Martin's funeral left the Government Hospital for the British cemetery by Hayat beach, attended by the District Commissioner, police commander James and the head of the CID, Officer Conquest.

ahr19461018-01.2.49.note: Ibrahim Mahmoud Assa of Kfar Wardiya, crushed by falling stone at a quarry, "gathered to the Government Hospital and there died."

ahr19461023-01.2.36.note: Yoachim Later (25, Romania), heart disease, to internal medicine; Janet Abramovitch (Romania), broken left leg from a fall; Shmuel Fikslen (21, Czechoslovakia). And a man who jumped into the sea and could not swim, revived after long treatment, returned to Atlit.

ahr19461101-01.2.64.note: Muhammad Hasan Attar (22) of Arab Mishaat, injured by a mine on the Hadera shore, "died an hour after he was brought there."

ahr19470121-01.2.32.note: And the reverse. Muhammad Abu Hamu, a café keeper, was murdered near midnight in the Arab market and his body taken to the Government Hospital. "A short while later some two hundred people, relatives and friends of the murdered man, came to the hospital, and finding the gate shut, climbed over the fence, entered the hospital, took the body out over the fence and brought it to his house. The matter was reported to the police, which sent a large armed guard to the hospital." A body that entered the register and left it again by the wall.

ahr19470209-01.2.47.note:
"The Government Hospital in Haifa reports four road accidents that occurred today, among them one fatality."

This is methodologically load-bearing and easy to miss. The names, ages, villages and injuries in these columns are not the reporter's own — they are the hospital's own bulletins, issued to the press. Press names and register names come from the same clerk. Where they agree, that is not corroboration but a single source seen twice; where they disagree, the difference is informative.

And the hospital's names were not always right. After the June 1946 railway workshops raid, HaBoker (hbkr19460619-01.2.9) notes that "the CID stuck names on the bodies, but they think the names are inaccurate."

ahr19470318-01.2.31.note: the shepherd Jamil Elias Abu Aksa threw a bomb he had found onto a rock at Mi'ilya; he was killed, and of the two young relatives with him, one — Kawkab, 11 — died at the Government Hospital and the other, Zakiya, was serious. The same column: Amina Ali al-Hilu, 80, of Kfar Yagur, run over in Nazareth Street.

ahr19470321-01.2.88.note: a bomb burst in the hands of a Jewish youth of about twenty in Sirkin Street; an army jeep took him to a military hospital and thence to the Government Hospital, "where an operation was performed on him." He is Yitzhak Buzaglo, 29, who left the hospital and was brought before the judge with both hands bandaged (hmf19470511-01.2.80).

ahr19470720-01.2.11.note:
"3 people were transferred to the Government Hospital and several sick people were taken to Atlit after being examined at the Government Hospital."

The Exodus, July 1947 (ahr19470720-01.2.11, hzh19470720-01.2.2, hmf19470721-01.2.4) — 4,389 deportees, 955 of them children; 28 sick and 34 of their relatives left in the country. "The sick sent to the Government Hospital are 17 men, 10 women and one child," with 34 relatives as escorts; 22 of them were then sent on to Atlit. Named among those who stayed: Aryeh Birenbaum (26), serious; William Milman (24), broken jaw; Ernst Weiss (24), chest wound on the left; Moshe Engelman. The dead: Zvi Yakubovitz (15), born in Bendin, Poland, of the Hancha children's kibbutz, whose brother had come before him and was in Atlit; Mordechai Baumstein (23); and a third who died in the hospital. "The dead were brought to the hospital half-naked." A woman died in childbirth — reportedly Pola Abramovitch — and her body was buried at sea. Of the wounded taken to the hospital, all were later moved to Atlit; six sick remained, "among them a girl of two ill with chickenpox, and her mother is with her."

On 21 July "three new graves were dug in the row of the martyrs of the ha'apala in the Haifa cemetery." At four in the afternoon a great crowd gathered beside the Government Hospital; the three bodies were brought out of the mortuary wrapped in blue-and-white flags and driven to the cemetery, Rabbi Dr Israel Goldstein eulogising.

Two men buried as "Abraham son of Abraham." On 11 February 1947 (dav19470212-01.2.6, hegeh19470212-01.2.8) the unknown ma'apil of the Lanegev, who died of wounds from the naval boarding, was buried from the Government Hospital in Bat Galim under that name — "the holy one who fell for the sanctification of the Name and of the Land." Nothing in his clothes identified him; his pockets held a comb in a leather case, a cigarette case and an empty notebook with a few unclear words. Minutes before the funeral a driver arrived saying he thought the dead man was his brother-in-law: Harry Laufer, born in Leipzig, a teacher of English, whose wife Barbara Seligman-Laufer had been deported to Cyprus with the rest. And in December 1946 (haretz19461206-01.2.74) the inquest on two Knesset Yisrael immigrants — Isaac Rosenbaum and an unknown "buried under the name Abraham son of Abraham" — heard "the testimony of the physician of the Government Hospital, who examined the bodies of the dead and performed autopsies on them," and found both died of army bullets, one to the head, one to the lungs and heart.

Anyone reading unnamed entries in the 1946–47 ledgers should know that this formula existed and what it covered.

ahr19471106-01.2.61.note:
under the heading "A grave accusation against the Government Hospital from the mouth of a judge":

"This is the second case brought before me in the last six weeks in which wounded men lose their lives through negligence on the part of the Government Hospital," said Judge Khalil Shehadeh today in the district court. "The treatment of poor people brought to the Government Hospital is not satisfactory; they discharge the patients before they have properly recovered. Had they been cured properly, it is possible they would have gone on living."

The case: Rashwan Awab, wounded in the head with a bottle and a knife in a quarrel over a room, was taken to the Government Hospital in January, left after a fortnight, and some weeks later his wounds suppurated; he was brought back and died there. The judge reduced his assailant's sentence "after the death was caused by the hospital's neglect."

A death recorded in the ledger, whose cause a court assigned to the institution itself. Worth holding beside any mortality figure drawn from the registers, and beside the discharge dates.

ahr19471111-01.2.74.note: Abdul Karim Nur, an employee of the Haifa health department, sentenced to fifteen years for shooting his wife Miriam; he drove her by taxi to the Government Hospital, "where she died the next day." A member of the Department of Health's own staff, and his wife an admission.

ahr19480209-01.2.80.note: "The Arabs in Haifa have opened a temporary hospital in the Abyad market beside the office of the Muslim Brothers." dav19360616-01.2.41.note: police fire one round at a man throwing stones from behind a tree; hit in the right leg, "carried by car to the Government Hospital in Haifa, but died on the way." The post-mortem gave shock and haemorrhage from the wound.

dav19370307-01.2.11.note: four Arabs preparing bombs in a house in the old city; the charge explodes at work, all four injured, two seriously, "all transferred to the Government Hospital."

dav19370618-01.2.93.note: "Work has begun on the building of the Government Hospital in Bat Galim. Some 80 Jewish and Arab workers are engaged in clearing the plot and in excavation." The first naming of the site in this corpus.

dav19370729-01.2.76.note: The Arab Workers' Society in Haifa protests the award of the hospital contract to a Jewish contractor, advising that the Government would do better to carry out the work itself.

dav19380221-01.2.46.note: - 1937-09-30 (dav19370930-01.2.91), 1938-02-03 (dav19380203-01.2.55, dav19380203-01.2.57), 1938-02-21 (dav19380221-01.2.46), 1938-05-08 (haretz19380508-01.2.25) [X] — Histadrut and Solel Boneh labour-market reporting in which the hospital site figures as a work-relief project. dav19380627-01.2.7.note: "late last night two armed men fired and killed an Arab within the grounds of the Government Hospital in Haifa." The hospital as a place where the violence reached, not only where it was treated.

dav19380704-01.2.13.note: a bomb thrown at a Hadar HaCarmel service car "on Mountain Road in the Herzliya quarter, beside the Government Hospital in Haifa." July 1938: the Mountain Road building is still the landmark, three months before the move.

dav19381116-01.2.35.2.note: 1938-11-16, Davar and Haaretz (dav19381116-01.2.35.2, haretz19381116-01.2.38.1) — A run of suppliers' advertisements: linoleum and rubber flooring, a carpentry cooperative that "executed all the joinery of the new Government Hospital building," mirrors and glazing, and Solel Boneh itself as "the contractor of the new Government Hospital building in Haifa." The trade ran its congratulations in mid-November, five weeks before the ceremony.

dav19381208-01.2.32.note: A polemic on the Jewish hospital in Haifa: still housed in a private building, without the primitive conditions a hospital needs, overcrowded beyond all bounds, with no department of internal medicine at all, and its numbers swollen by three years of disturbances. "After the completion of the Government Hospital building at Bat Galim, the deficiencies of our own hospital will stand out still more." Written a fortnight before the opening. It fixes what the Government Hospital meant locally: a standard against which the Yishuv measured its own provision and found it shaming.

dav19381220-01.2.77.note: "On Thursday the official opening of the new Government Hospital at Bat Galim, Haifa, will take place. The High Commissioner will be present."

dav19381222-01.2.83.note: "Yesterday afternoon the High Commissioner arrived in Haifa. This morning he will take part in the opening."

dav19381223-01.2.66.note: The fullest account of the ceremony. The building cost £120,000. "The plan of the hospital was drawn by the engineer Mr A. Mendelsohn." Five components: (1) a six-storey block for the beds and the nurses' quarters; (2) a three-storey block for operating theatres, outpatient reception and laboratory; (3) reception, first aid, offices and pharmacy; (4) the services wing; (5) the infectious-diseases wing. Extension is possible and there is ample room for a garden. £100,000 was allocated at first, raised to £112,000 as materials rose; 200 beds were provided for, then "24 beds were added for patients from among the military, and the budget was enlarged again." The High Commissioner's own speech says 225 beds, "befitting the needs of this city better than the old hospital building," and closes: "I declare the hospital officially open, and I wish that it may remain empty."

dav19381227-01.2.16.note: 1938-12-27, Davar, HaBoker, HaZman (dav19381227-01.2.16, hbkr19381227-01.2.17, hzh19381227-01.2.17) — The aftermath. The Va'ad Leumi writes to the Chief Secretary protesting that the speeches of the High Commissioner, the Director of Medical Services and the Mayor of Haifa "were not translated into Hebrew," which "gravely offended the feelings of the Jewish public, which sees in it a contempt for the recognised rights of the Hebrew language and for the dignity of the Yishuv." Three papers carried it; the opening was a language incident as much as a medical one.

dav19390620-01.2.4.note: 1939-06-19/20 — the Haifa market bomb. Four papers (dav19390620-01.2.4, dav19390620-01.2.44, hbkr19390620-01.2.18, hzh19390620-01.2.12). Lorries carried "piles of bodies to the Government Hospital." The dead and injured were partly from Balad al-Sheikh, partly from Haifa, "but there are also some from Safed and Jerusalem and from various villages." The funerals left from the Government Hospital at one in the afternoon: fifteen buried in the Muslim cemetery at Balad al-Sheikh, two taken for burial to Safed, one to Shefa-Amr. He is identified as the ma'apil taken with his wife near Migdal.

dav19470611-01.2.73.note: 1947-06-11/12 (dav19470611-01.2.73, hmf19470611-01.2.74, haretz19470612-01.2.39) — "Dr Laufer, a specialist surgeon who served during the war in the British army" — Haaretz adds "formerly chief surgeon in Abyssinia" — "has been appointed surgeon and deputy director of the Government Hospital in Haifa."

dav19470801-01.2.63.note: The trial, and it is worth reading in full. Hikmat Qasim, 22, married five years to Mustafa Abu Zahar, was childless; "all the treatment by Arab 'doctoresses' and midwives was of no use," and her husband threatened her. She had told him months earlier that she was pregnant. She took the baby, told the family she had given birth to a daughter, and told the judge she had meant to raise her as her own. The note that broke the case, left at the door of the baby's aunt on 16 May, read: "I have learned that Hikmat who lives in Wadi Rushmiya went with another woman on 10 May to the Government Hospital and they brought out a baby."

dav19470813-01.2.43.note: "Typhus in an Arab village. In the village of Kafrin, near Zichron Yaakov, a typhus epidemic has broken out. 25 of the villagers were transferred to a special department of the Government Hospital in Haifa. A quarantine has been imposed on the village." A datable mass admission of 25.

dav19471017-01.2.114.note: after a death aboard the Af Al Pi Chen: "again a day passed, and groups of mourners struck by disaster stood dark and wretched beside the Government Hospital in Haifa, a few hours after the sound of the blast had shaken the city, still asleep. The mourners were of the three communities, believers of three religions. So different in their dress, distinct in their language and in the shape of their world — and equal and united in their grief."

dav19480109-01.2.13.note: lays the blame on the Government, "in light of the fact that a Jewish doctor was murdered within the precincts of a government hospital (Dr Lehrs at the Government Hospital at Beit Safafa)." This identifies the murdered doctor of the January 1948 leader (dav19480109-01.2.13) that I set aside earlier as not-Haifa: it was Dr Lehrs at Beit Safafa, and the exclusion stands.

dav19480114-01.2.15.note: "Two unidentified bodies at the Government Hospital in Haifa. In the mortuary of the Government Hospital in Haifa lie two bodies, one found on Monday evening near Kfar Tira, the other brought from the east of the city. Anyone who knows of a missing Jew should apply to the Hevra Kadisha in Haifa (telephone 3923) or to the office in Hadar HaCarmel, Gilad Street." The mortuary advertised as a public identification service.

dav19480125-01.2.55.note: the same inquiry, angrier, and with two details HaMashkif omits: the Jewish staff's "pay was meagre" and their conditions poor, but "the hospital was made ownerless; the murderous gangs infused into it a spirit of terror. The health authorities did not heed the warnings, and when the employees felt their lives to be in danger they left. Together with them were taken out the few Jewish patients who were there in those days." And, on the day of the refinery riot, a British officer would not let the hospital's employees leave for Hadar HaCarmel "because of the danger of travelling by car," and moved them by police car to the nearby quarter.

dav19480205-01.2.9.note: police searching Jewish night-shift stevedores in the port; a police sergeant shot and killed one of them, Naftali Shlomovitz, 19, working on a tractor. "His body was transferred by the police at two in the night to the Government Hospital in Bat Galim."

dhy19310301-01.2.41.note: Murder trial of men of Daliyat al-Karmel before the Haifa district court. Among the witnesses, "a clerk of the Government Hospital and the nurse who treated the wounded woman." A named admission ought to sit behind this. Register lead.

dhy19310308-01.2.33.note: Haifa municipal council resolves "to allocate £100 towards paving part of the road beside the Government Hospital, as the Government requires." Mountain Road, and the Government pressing the municipality to pay for its approach.

dhy19320623-01.2.33.note: Under the heading "The arrangements of the Government Hospital": relatives of patients "complain bitterly that their sick lie in high fever for want of ice in the said hospital," and that the burden of fetching ice from town falls on the family. "Is such an arrangement to be the practice in a government hospital?" One of the few pieces here on conditions inside the wards rather than on admissions.

dhy19350912-01.2.71.note: The announcement. "Al-Muqattam reports that the Government intends to build a large government hospital in Haifa. The surgical department will hold 180 beds and the department for other diseases 80. The building work will begin shortly and will take two years." A 260-bed plan, announced September 1935, promised for 1937 — and the wards were not occupied until October 1938. Read against 1933-07-03, the deferral and its answer are now both on the record.

difaa19380707.note: The hospital-by-hospital tally printed the day after the Haifa market bombing of 6 July 1938. The register holds 34 injury admissions that day, of which one died — a 12-year-old Muslim boy with a bullet wound to chest and abdomen, admitted 6 July, died 7 July. 34 − 1 = 33, exactly the paper's count.
difaa19380707.orig: في مستشفى الحكومة: ٣٣ مصاباً بينهم ٧ في حالة خطرة
difaa19380707.trans: In the Government Hospital: 33 injured, among them 7 in critical condition.

difaa19460822.note: The one attestation that places the kerentina inside the hospital rather than beside it. Read against Filastin of 11 September 1941, which names the hospital, the health offices and the Kerentina as three distinct things, this is likelier loose usage — someone calling the hospital's own Isolation department “the quarantine.” See §08.
difaa19460822.orig: الى الكرنتينا في مستشفى الحكومة بحيفا
difaa19460822.trans: …to the quarantine in the Government Hospital in Haifa.

difaa19470507.note: The register has a man of 20 admitted 5 May 1947 and dead on 6 May, “Punc. W. Abdomen (Oper.) Bowel Injury”, notebook 31 page 33 — one of eleven Jewish men aged 17–33 with gunshot wounds after the Acre citadel prison break. Same day, same place, same outcome. The press supplies a name the register's redaction removed.
difaa19470507.orig: توفي في مستشفى الحكومة بحيفا صباح امس ارهابي جريح يدعى نسيم عبادي
difaa19470507.trans: There died in the Government Hospital in Haifa yesterday morning a wounded terrorist named Nasim ʿAbbadi.

haolam19370617-01.2.10.note: "The Government Department of Health has signed a contract with Solel Boneh for the building of the Government Hospital in Haifa. The building will cost some ninety thousand pounds; the installation work has been given to the Herut company. Among other conditions the Government stipulated that Solel Boneh employ 50 per cent Jews and 50 per cent Arabs. Work will begin in a few days."

haolam19371111-01.2.6.note: "Work on the building of the Government Hospital is advancing at a rapid pace. The work, valued at £100,000, is being done by Solel Boneh. Most of the workers were taken from among the unemployed. About 100 work daily."

haretz19330703-01.2.12.note: Annual review of health provision. "Because the enlargement of the Government Hospital in Haifa was deferred, the position there became difficult in the intestinal-disease season." Also: the eastern Galilee short of beds, patients falling back on the Scottish Mission hospital in Tiberias. Capacity, and a deferral that the 1935 announcement below finally answers.

haretz19331010-01.2.37.note: A passenger riding on the back of a lorry from Acre to Haifa struck by a passing vehicle, "died shortly after being brought to the Government Hospital." Register lead, early October 1933.

haretz19331217-01.2.23.note: The government hospital at Kerak, Transjordan, sold to the Italian mission. Not Haifa.

haretz19340125-01.2.53.1.note: Department of Health notice: public auction of a cart and mule at the Health Department office, "Mountain Road, by the Government Hospital." Fixes the address in the paper's own words, January 1934.

haretz19351002-01.2.100.1.note: 1935-08-12 (dav19350812-01.2.43), 1935-10-02 (haretz19351002-01.2.100.1), 1935-12-26 (dav19351226-01.2.73) [X] — a municipal labour agreement naming hospital costs generically, a physician's advertisement, and a projected government tuberculosis hospital. None is ours.

haretz19360608-01.2.83.note: At the trial of nine Arabs over the 1 May 1936 disturbances in Haifa and the killing of Dr S. Faderberg, "the evidence of the physicians of the Government Hospital": Dr Haddad and Dr N. Hamzeh, "physicians at the Government Hospital in Haifa." The first was called to the municipal police headquarters on 1 May and "saw many wounded there," then describes each accused man's injuries in turn.

haretz19360923-01.2.18.note: Dr Malchi, physician of the Government Hospital in Haifa, examined the body of Julia Koller, murdered near German Tira on 15 February, and found a fractured skull and internal haemorrhage in the ear and eye.

haretz19361016-01.2.59.3.note: A family's public thanks "to Dr A. Malchi, physician of the Government Hospital in Haifa, for his devoted treatment of our daughter and sister, who was saved from the grave and restored to life and health"; they are planting a tree in the Dizengoff forest in his name. A patient's family speaking in its own voice, which the registers never allow.

haretz19361023-01.2.53.note: Officer Halim Basta, head of the Haifa district police investigation office, wounded on 7 October in an attempt on his life, "left the Government Hospital yesterday, where he had been for about a fortnight," and is going on leave to Egypt. A named admission with both ends dated.

haretz19370214-01.2.17.note: Rashid Yasin of Jews' Street, wounded a month earlier and "only a few days ago left the Government Hospital," is bombed at his own door; he came down from his bed with his hand still bandaged and was unhurt.

haretz19370425-01.2.52.note: Dr Y. Shapira, physician of the Government Hospital in Haifa, opens a discussion on "sanitary and hygienic questions in industrial undertakings" for the Manufacturers' Association.

haretz19380120-01.2.72.1.note: a bar mitzvah invitation giving an address near the Government Hospital.

haretz19380508-01.2.25.note: - 1937-09-30 (dav19370930-01.2.91), 1938-02-03 (dav19380203-01.2.55, dav19380203-01.2.57), 1938-02-21 (dav19380221-01.2.46), 1938-05-08 (haretz19380508-01.2.25) [X] — Histadrut and Solel Boneh labour-market reporting in which the hospital site figures as a work-relief project. Real, and relevant to the building's economics, but not to the hospital as an institution.

haretz19380803-01.2.4.note: A bomb is thrown at a Jewish lorry "in which several Jewish workers employed on the building of the Government Hospital by Bat Galim were returning home," at the corner of Carmel Avenue and Allenby Street in the German Colony. It struck the worker Isser Tikovsky on the forehead and fell without exploding.

haretz19381116-01.2.38.1.note: 1938-11-16, Davar and Haaretz (dav19381116-01.2.35.2, haretz19381116-01.2.38.1) — A run of suppliers' advertisements: linoleum and rubber flooring, a carpentry cooperative that "executed all the joinery of the new Government Hospital building," mirrors and glazing, and Solel Boneh itself as "the contractor of the new Government Hospital building in Haifa." The trade ran its congratulations in mid-November, five weeks before the ceremony.

haretz19381223-01.2.5.note:
The same ceremony, with two things Davar does not carry. The institution's annual budget is put at about £20,000. And Dr Kampinsky, Mendelsohn's assistant, speaking in English, "gave details of the building work and said that its construction was completed in September of this year."

September finished, October occupied, December opened. The three dates now come from three independent directions — the architect's office, the registers, and the Government's own ceremony.

haretz19400102-01.2.84.note: "Dr A. Malchi, who served for many years as government physician in the Haifa district, has been appointed director of the government hospital for infectious diseases at Bnei Brak." Malchi runs from 1931 to 1940 through these pages — transferred in from Safed, doing the district's forensic work, thanked publicly by a patient's family, and out to a directorship.

haretz19430820-01.2.35.note: David Mabtsanik of Tiberias, 68, knocked down in Jaffa Street by an Arab public bus "of route number 5 (East Haifa — the Government Hospital)," died at Rothschild.

haretz19441003-01.2.34.note: - 1944-09-29 and 1944-10-03 (hazmantlv19440929-01.2.30, haretz19441003-01.2.34) — The British constable Arthur Whitley sentenced to six months for robbing £10 and a wristwatch from the body of Uzi Zahavi of Petah Tikva, run over in King's Street on 6 October 1943, "while he was transferring the body to the Government Hospital in Haifa." The conveyance of the dead was police work, and it was not always clean.

haretz19441117-01.2.59.note: two new cases — a man near the former Carmel station in the west, a woman at Balad al-Sheikh by Yagur. Since 20 June: 64 cases, 18 dead, 36 recovered, 10 still in hospital

haretz19450123-01.2.35.note: an Arab porter pumping water from a cellar in King's Street touches a faulty electric lamp and is electrocuted; "his body was transferred to the mortuary beside the Government Hospital. His identity has not yet been established."

haretz19450401-01.2.32.note: "Dr A. Malchi, director of the Government Hospital, has returned from his journey to Egypt on behalf of the Department of Health and resumed his duties." Malchi runs right through this corpus: transferred in from Safed in 1931, the district's forensic physician through the 1930s, thanked in an advertisement by a patient's family in 1936, out in 1940 to direct the infectious-diseases hospital at Bnei Brak — and back by 1945 as director of the Haifa hospital itself.

haretz19450510-01.2.26.note: a retrospective on a bombardment: 39 killed and 78 wounded, "most of them Muslims," the refineries hit; "the men of Magen David Adom distinguished themselves, helping the staff of the Government Hospital whose hands were full of work; two Jewish surgeons were also sent at the request of the management of that hospital." The event is one of the earlier raids, not a 1945 one — worth dating before use, but the detail of the hospital asking for outside surgeons is good.

haretz19450710-01.2.24.note: A review of the Public Works Department's wartime building. Under "The war against the plague epidemic": "The Department of Public Works took part in the operations against the plague epidemic. In 1942 the Department set up a special department for plague sufferers beside the Government Hospital in Haifa, and in the same year an isolation pavilion of 14 beds was built for the government hospital at Beit Safafa near Jerusalem." Further down, among the war years' works, "to the Government Hospital in Haifa a pavilion of 20 beds was added."

haretz19451023-01.2.20.note:
A reorganisation of the bus co-operatives: "the cars of number 7 run from Bat Galim via the Government Hospital to the eastern railway station," and there is a Hadar HaCarmel — Bat Galim service much used in summer.

Two named routes, seven years apart, both terminating on the hospital. Between 1943 and 1945 it is a fixed point of the municipal transport map.

haretz19451118-01.2.31.note: - 1945-11-18 (haretz19451118-01.2.31), 1945-11-30 (haretz19451130-01.2.52), 1945-01-23 (first window) [X] — Magen David Adom columns whose casualties go to Rothschild.

haretz19451130-01.2.52.note: - 1945-11-18 (haretz19451118-01.2.31), 1945-11-30 (haretz19451130-01.2.52), 1945-01-23 (first window) [X] — Magen David Adom columns whose casualties go to Rothschild.

haretz19451211-01.2.55.note: "Dr Ibrahim Isa'is of Nablus has been appointed deputy director of the Government Hospital in Haifa, in place of Dr Mishlani, who has been appointed director of the Government Hospital in Nablus. Dr Isa'is began work yesterday." Two named Arab physicians in the senior posts, and the government hospitals working as a single service with transfers between them.

haretz19460905-01.2.21.note: the best single list. Of 45 sick immigrants left in the country, 39 went to the Jewish Agency's hospital at Atlit and six to the Government Hospital, named with their departments: 1) Tzipora Moskovitz; 2) Leah Kling, 26, from Germany, in the maternity department; 3) Berta Perlstein; …; 5) Moshe Weisel, from Romania, 23, in the surgical department, "wounded in the head during the clash with the sailors of the destroyer Childers when they boarded the Four Freedoms"; 6) Moshe Lazar, also Romanian, in the infectious-diseases department, suspected of tuberculosis.

haretz19460911-01.2.25.note: a British CID sergeant shot by the Windsor Hotel, hit in seven places, "gathered to the Government Hospital and there died"; Sergeant Martin's funeral left the Government Hospital for the British cemetery by Hayat beach, attended by the District Commissioner, police commander James and the head of the CID, Officer Conquest.

haretz19461206-01.2.74.note:
"3 people were transferred to the Government Hospital and several sick people were taken to Atlit after being examined at the Government Hospital."

The Exodus, July 1947 (ahr19470720-01.2.11, hzh19470720-01.2.2, hmf19470721-01.2.4) — 4,389 deportees, 955 of them children; 28 sick and 34 of their relatives left in the country. "The sick sent to the Government Hospital are 17 men, 10 women and one child," with 34 relatives as escorts; 22 of them were then sent on to Atlit. Named among those who stayed: Aryeh Birenbaum (26), serious; William Milman (24), broken jaw; Ernst Weiss (24), chest wound on the left; Moshe Engelman. The dead: Zvi Yakubovitz (15), born in Bendin, Poland, of the Hancha children's kibbutz, whose brother had come before him and was in Atlit; Mordechai Baumstein (23); and a third who died in the hospital. "The dead were brought to the hospital half-naked." A woman died in childbirth — reportedly Pola Abramovitch — and her body was buried at sea. Of the wounded taken to the hospital, all were later moved to Atlit; six sick remained, "among them a girl of two ill with chickenpox, and her mother is with her."

On 21 July "three new graves were dug in the row of the martyrs of the ha'apala in the Haifa cemetery." At four in the afternoon a great crowd gathered beside the Government Hospital; the three bodies were brought out of the mortuary wrapped in blue-and-white flags and driven to the cemetery, Rabbi Dr Israel Goldstein eulogising.

Two men buried as "Abraham son of Abraham." On 11 February 1947 (dav19470212-01.2.6, hegeh19470212-01.2.8) the unknown ma'apil of the Lanegev, who died of wounds from the naval boarding, was buried from the Government Hospital in Bat Galim under that name — "the holy one who fell for the sanctification of the Name and of the Land." Nothing in his clothes identified him; his pockets held a comb in a leather case, a cigarette case and an empty notebook with a few unclear words. Minutes before the funeral a driver arrived saying he thought the dead man was his brother-in-law: Harry Laufer, born in Leipzig, a teacher of English, whose wife Barbara Seligman-Laufer had been deported to Cyprus with the rest. And in December 1946 (haretz19461206-01.2.74) the inquest on two Knesset Yisrael immigrants — Isaac Rosenbaum and an unknown "buried under the name Abraham son of Abraham" — heard "the testimony of the physician of the Government Hospital, who examined the bodies of the dead and performed autopsies on them," and found both died of army bullets, one to the head, one to the lungs and heart.

Anyone reading unnamed entries in the 1946–47 ledgers should know that this formula existed and what it covered.

haretz19470119-01.2.56.note: - 1947-01-19/22, 1947-02-02 (haretz19470119-01.2.56, hbkr19470122-01.2.38, haretz19470122-01.2.62, haretz19470202-01.2.36) — after the bombing of the Haifa police fortress on 12 January 1947, fifteen wounded were still in the Government Hospital ten days later: five Arab supernumerary constables, one Egyptian cook and nine English policemen, some in serious condition. The last Arab supernumerary left three weeks after the explosion, "in the hospital there remain only some British policemen." A ward census by community, from the press.

haretz19470122-01.2.62.note: - 1947-01-19/22, 1947-02-02 (haretz19470119-01.2.56, hbkr19470122-01.2.38, haretz19470122-01.2.62, haretz19470202-01.2.36) — after the bombing of the Haifa police fortress on 12 January 1947, fifteen wounded were still in the Government Hospital ten days later: five Arab supernumerary constables, one Egyptian cook and nine English policemen, some in serious condition. The last Arab supernumerary left three weeks after the explosion, "in the hospital there remain only some British policemen." A ward census by community, from the press.

haretz19470202-01.2.36.note: - 1947-01-19/22, 1947-02-02 (haretz19470119-01.2.56, hbkr19470122-01.2.38, haretz19470122-01.2.62, haretz19470202-01.2.36) — after the bombing of the Haifa police fortress on 12 January 1947, fifteen wounded were still in the Government Hospital ten days later: five Arab supernumerary constables, one Egyptian cook and nine English policemen, some in serious condition. The last Arab supernumerary left three weeks after the explosion, "in the hospital there remain only some British policemen." A ward census by community, from the press.

haretz19470612-01.2.39.note: 1947-06-11/12 (dav19470611-01.2.73, hmf19470611-01.2.74, haretz19470612-01.2.39) — "Dr Laufer, a specialist surgeon who served during the war in the British army" — Haaretz adds "formerly chief surgeon in Abyssinia" — "has been appointed surgeon and deputy director of the Government Hospital in Haifa."

haretz19470701-01.2.45.note: "According to the announcement of the Government Hospital in Haifa, those hit by the soldiers' fire on Sunday evening were the Arab boy Mahmoud Ahmad Muhammad, 13, and the Arab Rushd Salal Ahmad, 30. The first, who works in a bakery, was hit in the leg; the second, who happened to be passing in the street, was hit in the neck."

haretz19470807-01.2.69.note: "All the plague patients from Haifa have left the Government Hospital in Haifa, apart from 3 patients transferred some time ago from Afula." The end of the outbreak charted in the 1942–45 section.

haretz19471125-01.2.27.note: Sergeant Kiely, "the Hebrew expert of the Haifa CID," wounded in the attack at the Haz café on 12 November, recovered and left the Government Hospital.

haretz19480123-01.2.61.note: "A headless body found. In the mortuary of the Government Hospital in Haifa a body without a head has lain for some days. On the body is a khaki shirt; the underclothes are dark. It has not yet been possible to determine whether the body is a Jew's or an Arab's."

haretz19480209-01.2.44.note: "The Arabs in Haifa have opened a temporary hospital in the Abyad market beside the office of the Muslim Brothers." And by February the Arab hospital al-Amin in the east of the city is named repeatedly (ahr19480209-01.2.80, haretz19480209-01.2.44, hzh19480209-01.2.11) — the International Red Cross delegation of 8 February toured the MDA station, Rothschild, Beit Borochov, the Government Hospital and al-Amin.

haretz19480428-01.2.48.note:
1948-04-28, four papers (haretz19480428-01.2.48, hbkr19480428-01.2.44, hmf19480428-01.2.57, hzh19480428-01.2.24) — Six days after the fall of Arab Haifa, Dr A. Katznelson, director of the Va'ad Leumi's health department, with his deputy Dr B. Hirshovitz and Dr Y. Meir of the emergency medical committee, came to Haifa. A district health committee was set up under Dr B. Nissenbaum. "In a meeting with Dr McLean, director of the government health office, and Dr Hamzi, director of the Government Hospital, Dr Katznelson announced the institutions' decision to ensure the orderly continuation of the Government Hospital for the benefit of the population in general and the Arab population in particular, and asked the Arab personnel to continue their work without any fears. There is no justification for the abandonment of the institution by the Arab patients and wounded, and the Jewish institutions are ready for their part to give the institution all necessary help."

Dr Hamzi is Dr N. Hamzeh — the physician of the Government Hospital who gave evidence at the trial over the 1 May 1936 disturbances, and who in December 1940 tried to separate the conjoined twins from Shefa-Amr. Twelve years in these pages, ending as director.

haretz19480503-01.2.39.note:
the closing scene, and the terminus of the whole register.

"The Government Hospital in Haifa — to the municipality. (From our correspondent in Haifa) The Government Hospital in Haifa was transferred yesterday to the authority of the Haifa municipality and will serve from now on as a municipal hospital. This hospital contains 288 beds and is one of the largest and finest hospitals in the country. For the present there will be opened in it a department for infectious diseases, a surgical department and a clinic for the Arab population… "Our correspondent, who visited the hospital yesterday, found it completely empty. Apart from the joint guard of Jews and British policemen, a few individual British doctors and British nurses, there is not a living soul in it. He was told that immediately upon the conquest of Haifa the Arab employees and patients began to leave the hospital in masses. Many patients were transferred by ambulance to the environs of Haifa, many others were taken by boat to Acre. About 60 Arabs, the last of the patients, were taken out of the hospital last Thursday. With them went the last of the nurses, most of them Armenian. The Arab doctors also left… "Despite his personal promise, Dr Hamzi's ambulances did not return. Dr Hamzi has left for Lebanon. By contrast, praise is due to the conduct of the British chief physician, Dr MacNeil, and of the property inspector, Mr Dook (an Arab, a British subject), thanks to whom the equipment stores were preserved intact. "The interior of the hospital arouses nausea. The great halls, formerly gleaming with cleanliness, are filthy and befouled. Here and there stretchers still lie stained with blood. In the mortuary four Arab bodies were still lying last night. The beds are overturned; in the nurses' room there is no sign of order. In several departments part of the equipment is missing."

haretz19480504-01.2.42.note: 1948-05-04, six papers (ahr19480504-01.2.34, ahr19480504-01.2.75, haretz19480504-01.2.42, hmf19480504-01.2.48, khm19480504-01.2.49, mar19480504-01.2.7) — the Va'ad Leumi declared the Jewish institutions ready "to take upon themselves the care also of the Arab patients and wounded who are in the hospital," and put £10,000 at the municipality's disposal to ease the transfer. HaMashkif's one-liner adds that the transfer was made "under the auspices of the International Red Cross."

haretz19480507-01.2.59.note: "The mayor of Haifa, Mr Shabtai Levy, appealed to all the Arab employees of the Government Hospital and to the employees of the land registry department to return to their work, and said that he is responsible for their personal safety."

hashaah19400923-01.2.15.note:
1940-09-20 — the heavy raid. (hbkr19400922-01.2.39, hashaah19400923-01.2.15) The tin roof of a café collapsed on those inside. "Magen David Adom sent several surgeons and physicians to the Government Hospital." A wounded bus driver could not go on driving and "a British constable rushed to the wheel and drove the bus to the Government Hospital." And the detail that matters most here: "13 of the victims of the bombardment were not buried at once because they were not identified. When they were identified they were buried in the cemetery at Balad al-Sheikh. Four more victims remained unidentified." Unnamed entries in the ledger for late September 1940 have an explanation waiting for them.

1940-11/12 — the Patria. (hbkr19401127-01.2.21, hmf19401205-01.2.9) "At the Government Hospital another woman died yesterday, of those gathered into the institution on Monday immediately after the disaster." All surviving refugees were then moved to the detention camp; bodies recovered from the water in December went "straight to the mortuary of the Government Hospital," with 41 buried by 5 December. This is the Haifa end of the Atlit camp register, Notebook 25 — the same catastrophe, the other institution.

hashaharerev19401227-01.2.11.note: 1940-12-27, HaShahar (hashaharerev19401227-01.2.11) and 1940-12-29, HaBoker (hbkr19401229-01.2.54) — Conjoined twins born at Shefa-Amr to Amida Fadl-Allah, joined at the liver, "taken to the maternity department of the Government Hospital in Haifa" and fed artificially. "The chief physician, Dr J. H. Thomson, and Dr Naif Hamzeh" sought to separate them. Two days later they died; "the government physicians who treated this strange creature were sure in advance that they would not live long. Their mother, Falhiya of the village of Shefa-Amr, is entirely well and is at home." A named chief physician for 1940, a named Arab physician still in post four years after his 1936 court testimony, and the maternity department named as such.

hayomjlm19480304-01.2.42.note: the Stanton Street car bomb: "ambulances of the Government Hospital and of the Red Cross rushed to the place and transferred the casualties to the military and Arab hospitals" — not, by this account, to the Government Hospital itself.

hazmantlv19430830-01.2.40.note: the supernumerary constable Abdallah Hasan Mahmoud began to drown while bathing in Haifa Bay; the other bathers pulled him out "while the breath was still in him" and he went unconscious to the Government Hospital.

hazmantlv19430903-01.2.20.note: Abd al-Latif Rashid shot in the neck in an alley of the Arab market; "transferred in a critical condition to the Government Hospital and consciousness has not yet returned to him."

hazmantlv19431208-01.2.44.note: Ephraim Kassan, 15, son of a Kupat Holim doctor at Kfar Ata, run over at the Haifa–Acre crossroads by a police car and in the same instant by a military lorry; died minutes later, "before they had time to render him first aid"; body to the Government Hospital for examination.

hazmantlv19431229-01.2.45.note: two Arab workers quarrel at a camp; a third tries to make peace, fails to persuade them "by the sayings of his mouth," picks up an iron bar and swings it into the face of one of them, who goes seriously injured to the Government Hospital. "The peacemaker" was arrested.

hazmantlv19440116-01.2.59.note: over cards at Kurdani camp, Fawzi al-Shami of Damascus stabs Turki al-Qaud to death; the body is gathered to the Government Hospital.

hazmantlv19440124-01.2.41.note: an army car and a full Arab bus collide on the Haifa–Acre road near Kiryat Hashmal; six passengers injured including the driver Ahmad Yusuf Abed, all to the Government Hospital; and, the same day, a supernumerary Arab constable injured in a third accident.

hazmantlv19440131-01.2.34.note: the body of Shlomo Yaakov Halabi found in King's Street; gathered to the Government Hospital; "by the marks they suppose he was run over by an unknown car."

hazmantlv19440525-01.2.20.note: "There exists in Haifa a large and spacious government hospital, which the Jewish yishuv generally has no need of." By contrast Rothschild is the only place of hospitalisation for the Jewish sector of Haifa and its immediate district. Its figures, for comparison with the Government Hospital's 133.5: a surgical department of 37 beds, a children's department of 13, a maternity department of 7 besides 25 maternity beds moved to the old Hadassah building on Hadar HaCarmel; a budget of £25,000 and over; a staff of 8 doctors and 54 permanent employees "including 32 nurses."

hazmantlv19440914-01.2.26.note: the trial of the Bedouin woman Sara Hussein, charged with abandoning her day-old illegitimate daughter in Nazareth Street in March. Police found the baby wrapped in rags at the roadside "and brought her into the Government Hospital." In court the mother said she had wanted to avoid shame, "clasped her small daughter and broke into bitter weeping," and the sentence was reduced. The second foundling in this corpus (see 1939-04-23), and this one has a name, a date and an outcome.

hazmantlv19440929-01.2.30.note: - 1944-09-29 and 1944-10-03 (hazmantlv19440929-01.2.30, haretz19441003-01.2.34) — The British constable Arthur Whitley sentenced to six months for robbing £10 and a wristwatch from the body of Uzi Zahavi of Petah Tikva, run over in King's Street on 6 October 1943, "while he was transferring the body to the Government Hospital in Haifa." The conveyance of the dead was police work, and it was not always clean.

hbkr19351021-01.2.85.note: A feud between two families at Ein Hod turns into a pitched fight, 37 taking part; "eight of the combatants were injured and gathered to the Government Hospital in Haifa," two of them seriously. Register lead — a datable multiple admission.

hbkr19351105-01.2.51.note: The body of the sailor Muhammad al-Manbi, lost with a Syrian boat and washed ashore near Kfar Samir, "was taken for examination to the Government Hospital in Haifa." The hospital as the district mortuary — a function the registers do not record.

hbkr19351119-01.2.79.note: The Northern District Governor goes to the Government Hospital in Jerusalem for treatment of an eye.

hbkr19380225-01.2.40.note: A civic address noting with satisfaction that "the new Government Hospital will open shortly," alongside a new government trades school and the coast road, and complaining that large areas of unfit housing remain "a danger to health."

hbkr19380315-01.2.22.note: 1938-03-15 (hbkr19380315-01.2.22), 1938-05-11 (hbkr19380511-01.2.71, hzh19380511-01.2.43) — The Haifa municipal budget and council resolutions provide £800 "to pave the road leading to the new Government Hospital near Bat Galim," to be executed by the municipality's own technical department, using only cement from the Nesher works. The approach road is municipal; the hospital is not.

hbkr19380511-01.2.71.note: 1938-03-15 (hbkr19380315-01.2.22), 1938-05-11 (hbkr19380511-01.2.71, hzh19380511-01.2.43) — The Haifa municipal budget and council resolutions provide £800 "to pave the road leading to the new Government Hospital near Bat Galim," to be executed by the municipality's own technical department, using only cement from the Nesher works. The approach road is municipal; the hospital is not.

hbkr19381104-01.2.55.note: Ali Arif Jubran, trying to throw a bomb in the Abyad market, has it burst in his hand; the police gather him up and take him "to the Government Hospital in Haifa," and the fragments to the laboratory. Dated 3 November 1938 — after the move, so this one tests the seam.

hbkr19381118-01.2.28.note:
The load-bearing article. A full description, and it is written in the present tense about a working hospital. In June [1937] the erection of the huge building began, on a site of 60 dunam west of Haifa port; the plot was purchased by the Government for some £41,000 (its prior designation is unreadable in the OCR). Of the equipment "transferred from the old hospital," over £10,000 more was spent on new installation. Around the main building stand pavilions for infectious diseases and others, joined to it by a special roofed passage. "In all the Government Hospital has for the present 230 beds, among them 90 for infectious diseases." And: "of the 110 employees at the Government Hospital there is a very small percentage of Jewish employees."

This is dated five weeks before the opening ceremony and describes equipment already moved and beds already counted. It is independent confirmation, from outside the registers, that the hospital was working at Bat Galim well before 22 December — consistent with the October 1938 NB20→NB21 seam and inconsistent with reading the December ceremony as the move.

hbkr19381223-01.2.57.note: Mendelsohn was not at his own opening: the Director of Government Medical Services read out the architect's letter expressing his regret at being absent, having taken leave. The speakers stress the harmony between Jewish and Arab workers on the site, and that the building was completed within the required time.

hbkr19381227-01.2.17.note: 1938-12-27, Davar, HaBoker, HaZman (dav19381227-01.2.16, hbkr19381227-01.2.17, hzh19381227-01.2.17) — The aftermath. The Va'ad Leumi writes to the Chief Secretary protesting that the speeches of the High Commissioner, the Director of Medical Services and the Mayor of Haifa "were not translated into Hebrew," which "gravely offended the feelings of the Jewish public, which sees in it a contempt for the recognised rights of the Hebrew language and for the dignity of the Yishuv." Three papers carried it; the opening was a language incident as much as a medical one.

hbkr19390620-01.2.18.note: 1939-06-19/20 — the Haifa market bomb. Four papers (dav19390620-01.2.4, dav19390620-01.2.44, hbkr19390620-01.2.18, hzh19390620-01.2.12). Lorries carried "piles of bodies to the Government Hospital." The dead and injured were partly from Balad al-Sheikh, partly from Haifa, "but there are also some from Safed and Jerusalem and from various villages." The funerals left from the Government Hospital at one in the afternoon: fifteen buried in the Muslim cemetery at Balad al-Sheikh, two taken for burial to Safed, one to Shefa-Amr. And a story the registers cannot tell: a Jewish pedlar, Alfred Hahn (27) — Davar first prints Cohen and corrects itself in the same issue — went into "the mortuary of the Government Hospital in Haifa, where the victims of the explosion were lying," was set upon by Arab women and stabbed in the back; he was moved to Hadassah. HaBoker has his own account: he had gone to the Government Hospital to get medical treatment for his own illness, having no money in his pocket, knew nothing of what had happened in the town, and was attacked in the hospital yard. He is identified as the ma'apil taken with his wife near Migdal.

hbkr19390925-01.2.32.note: a road accident near Afula; the injured wardress taken to the government hospital at Bethlehem.

hbkr19391012-01.2.51.1.note: a flat to let in Pardes Katz "behind the Government Hospital," i.e. Tel Aviv's.

hbkr19400101-01.2.81.note:
A digest of the Department of Health's annual report for 1938, with the average number of beds occupied daily. Across all government hospitals, 771. Within that:

| institution | avg. beds occupied daily, 1938 | |---|---:| | Tel Aviv municipal (counted as governmental for the subsidy) | 290.5 | | Government Hospital, Haifa | 133.5 | | Nablus | 97.6 | | Jaffa | 91 | | Jerusalem | 90.8 | | Hadassah Jerusalem (voluntary) | 181.2 | | Beilinson (voluntary) | 102.2 | | Hadassah Haifa (voluntary) | 67.5 |

133.5 beds occupied on an average day in 1938, in a building rated first at 200 and then 224–225. This is directly comparable to the registers and belongs beside the Blue Book series in the register's annual serial count. Note that it straddles the move: 1938 is the last Mountain Road year and the first Bat Galim months.

hbkr19400110-01.2.22.note: Government estimates: £4,913 for furniture and equipment of the Government Hospital in Haifa. The same column notes that in the mental hospitals Jews were a majority — 83 against 73 Arabs — "a very sad majority."

hbkr19400807-01.2.14.note: 1940-08-06 — an air raid. (hbkr19400807-01.2.14) The Arab Sa'id Ibrahim killed; Ali Masri, Muhammad Hasan and Wadi' al-Shukri wounded, "all transferred to the Government Hospital," Ali Masri seriously. The Jewish workers lightly wounded by splinters were dressed at Hadassah and sent home — four named. The same event, two hospitals, sorted by community.

hbkr19400820-01.2.36.note: the American vice-consul in Beirut, Mr Wightman, and Brigadier-General McNeil, hurt when their cars collided near Acre, "left the Government Hospital in Haifa yesterday, where the necessary medical assistance was rendered them."

hbkr19400922-01.2.39.note:
1940-09-20 — the heavy raid. (hbkr19400922-01.2.39, hashaah19400923-01.2.15) The tin roof of a café collapsed on those inside. "Magen David Adom sent several surgeons and physicians to the Government Hospital." A wounded bus driver could not go on driving and "a British constable rushed to the wheel and drove the bus to the Government Hospital." And the detail that matters most here: "13 of the victims of the bombardment were not buried at once because they were not identified. When they were identified they were buried in the cemetery at Balad al-Sheikh. Four more victims remained unidentified." Unnamed entries in the ledger for late September 1940 have an explanation waiting for them.

1940-11/12 — the Patria. (hbkr19401127-01.2.21, hmf19401205-01.2.9) "At the Government Hospital another woman died yesterday, of those gathered into the institution on Monday immediately after the disaster." All surviving refugees were then moved to the detention camp; bodies recovered from the water in December went "straight to the mortuary of the Government Hospital," with 41 buried by 5 December. This is the Haifa end of the Atlit camp register, Notebook 25 — the same catastrophe, the other institution.

hbkr19401229-01.2.54.note: 1940-12-27, HaShahar (hashaharerev19401227-01.2.11) and 1940-12-29, HaBoker (hbkr19401229-01.2.54) — Conjoined twins born at Shefa-Amr to Amida Fadl-Allah, joined at the liver, "taken to the maternity department of the Government Hospital in Haifa" and fed artificially. "The chief physician, Dr J. H. Thomson, and Dr Naif Hamzeh" sought to separate them. Two days later they died; "the government physicians who treated this strange creature were sure in advance that they would not live long. Their mother, Falhiya of the village of Shefa-Amr, is entirely well and is at home." A named chief physician for 1940, a named Arab physician still in post four years after his 1936 court testimony, and the maternity department named as such.

hbkr19410325-01.2.30.note: a boy of about 13 on a bicycle in Prophets' Street goes under the wheels of a heavy lorry; "his body was taken to the Government Hospital and the police opened an inquiry." Attempts to identify him failed "because the boy's head was crushed in such a way that his features could not be made out. The only thing found on him was a letter from the Hashomer Hatzair branch in Rehovot to a girl."

hbkr19410805-01.2.21.note: an iron plate falls on an Arab labourer at Haifa port; hand badly injured; brought by Magen David Adom car to the Government Hospital.

hbkr19410825-01.2.28.note: Sergeant Allen of the army, struck by a car by Hayat beach, seriously hurt, to the Government Hospital.

hbkr19410829-01.2.47.note: a lorry hits Arab children playing at a street corner in Wadi Rushmiya; two lightly hurt and taken home, "the third, more seriously hurt, was transferred to the Government Hospital in Haifa." The same column sends a Jewish port worker with a crushed leg to Kupat Holim instead — the sorting is visible in a single paragraph.

hbkr19410903-01.2.31.note: a woman struck by an army car crossing King's Street, taken to the Government Hospital.

hbkr19410926-01.2.58.note: Officer John Wicomb [?] of the Haifa police, out on the night of Thursday with a police guard towards Acre on the track of a band of smugglers, fired on at the village of Sha'ab and shot in the abdomen. "He was transferred at once to the Government Hospital and there he was operated upon, but they did not succeed in saving his life." He came to the country in 1934, served in the Jerusalem police and had been transferred to Haifa only months before. His funeral was to leave from the Government Hospital at three that afternoon. An admission, an operation, a death and a departure, all datable.

hbkr19420624-01.2.52.note: A Government tender for medical stores for the four months August–November 1942. Bids were invited for "(a) the whole country; (b) the whole country except Haifa; (c) for the Government Hospital in Haifa alone." Haifa was large enough to be its own procurement unit.

hbkr19421029-01.2.19.note: The ten-year history of getting Rothschild built, opening on the claim that "the Jewish hospital together with the Government Hospital have solved the hospitalisation distress completely." PICA gave four dunams on Herzl Street and the Government added half a dunam of its own adjoining it; the 1934 plan was approved and then abandoned as too central and too small; ten dunams were bought on the flank of the Carmel; plans went in in December 1940 and were approved; and "in the middle of 1941, with the beginning of the bombardment from the air," the Government approved the plan and issued a licence for scarce building materials. Engineers Rozov–Woltsch.

hbkr19440301-01.2.42.note: In the Tel Aviv debate: "there is a government hospital for Haifa, Jaffa, Nablus and other places, and only great Tel Aviv has not been granted a government hospital." The Haifa institution as the thing other cities wanted.

hbkr19440601-01.2.37.note:
"Yesterday there died in the quarantine house beside the Government Hospital in Haifa Eliezer ―――, aged 32. It is feared that death came from smallpox."

Together with the 1944–45 plague reporting below, which consistently sends patients to "the isolation unit (מבדדה)", "the department for infectious diseases of the Government Hospital" and "the department for infectious diseases beside the Government Hospital," this bears directly on the question of Haifa's lazaret. For plague and smallpox in 1942–45 the isolation facility was built by the Government at the hospital and operated as part of it, not at a separate lazaret elsewhere in the town. That does not dissolve the الكرنتينا / المحجر الصحي of the Arabic sources — a port quarantine station is a different institution with a different job — but it removes the hypothesis that Haifa's plague and smallpox cases went somewhere the register cannot see. For these years the register plausibly is the denominator. The open question should be narrowed accordingly rather than left standing.

hbkr19460619-01.2.9.note:
"The Government Hospital in Haifa reports four road accidents that occurred today, among them one fatality."

This is methodologically load-bearing and easy to miss. The names, ages, villages and injuries in these columns are not the reporter's own — they are the hospital's own bulletins, issued to the press. Press names and register names come from the same clerk. Where they agree, that is not corroboration but a single source seen twice; where they disagree, the difference is informative.

And the hospital's names were not always right. After the June 1946 railway workshops raid, HaBoker (hbkr19460619-01.2.9) notes that "the CID stuck names on the bodies, but they think the names are inaccurate."

hbkr19460703-01.2.4.note: the 1,108 immigrants of the Biriya held aboard under quarantine; "after three suspected plague cases were transferred to a special department of the Government Hospital," disinfection with DDT began and the transfer to Atlit proceeded. Three of them told the medical delegation that visited them at the hospital: "we don't care if it's plague or not — what does it matter? The main thing is that we reached where we wanted." The examination proved negative.

hbkr19460901-01.2.33.note: Yehudit Weinstein moved from the Atlit camp to the isolation department.

hbkr19460911-01.2.51.note: "An attempt to break into the Government Hospital in Haifa by armed youths was foiled yesterday at 10.15 in the morning. The attackers, who appeared in Arab dress in a car, aroused the suspicion of the guard posted beside the hospital," and fled towards Hadera when police reinforcements arrived.

hbkr19470122-01.2.38.note: - 1947-01-19/22, 1947-02-02 (haretz19470119-01.2.56, hbkr19470122-01.2.38, haretz19470122-01.2.62, haretz19470202-01.2.36) — after the bombing of the Haifa police fortress on 12 January 1947, fifteen wounded were still in the Government Hospital ten days later: five Arab supernumerary constables, one Egyptian cook and nine English policemen, some in serious condition. The last Arab supernumerary left three weeks after the explosion, "in the hospital there remain only some British policemen." A ward census by community, from the press.

hbkr19480129-01.2.90.note:
"The Government Hospital in Haifa abandoned by the Jews under pressure," and then a partial return: "A late report says: eight Jewish doctors at the Government Hospital in Haifa, and 20 clerks who work in the health department there, returned yesterday to their work. The nurses and Jewish trainee nurses have not yet returned. A guard of eight British policemen and two [Arab] policemen has been posted there."

So: patients and staff out on 31 December 1947, doctors and clerks back around 28 January 1948, nurses not. Any discontinuity in the ledgers across that seam now has a documented cause and a date on either side.

hbkr19480428-01.2.44.note:
1948-04-28, four papers (haretz19480428-01.2.48, hbkr19480428-01.2.44, hmf19480428-01.2.57, hzh19480428-01.2.24) — Six days after the fall of Arab Haifa, Dr A. Katznelson, director of the Va'ad Leumi's health department, with his deputy Dr B. Hirshovitz and Dr Y. Meir of the emergency medical committee, came to Haifa. A district health committee was set up under Dr B. Nissenbaum. "In a meeting with Dr McLean, director of the government health office, and Dr Hamzi, director of the Government Hospital, Dr Katznelson announced the institutions' decision to ensure the orderly continuation of the Government Hospital for the benefit of the population in general and the Arab population in particular, and asked the Arab personnel to continue their work without any fears. There is no justification for the abandonment of the institution by the Arab patients and wounded, and the Jewish institutions are ready for their part to give the institution all necessary help."

Dr Hamzi is Dr N. Hamzeh — the physician of the Government Hospital who gave evidence at the trial over the 1 May 1936 disturbances, and who in December 1940 tried to separate the conjoined twins from Shefa-Amr. Twelve years in these pages, ending as director.

hegeh19440427-01.2.17.note: 1944-04-27, Davar and HaGeh (dav19440427-01.2.40, hegeh19440427-01.2.17) — The Palestine Broadcasting Service schedule: at 8.00 p.m., "a 'By Request' programme specially for the nurses of the Government Hospital in Haifa." The nursing staff as a public, named on air.

hegeh19440906-01.2.23.note: "the 22nd case of plague in Haifa" — an Arab of Allenby Street; 8 of the sick have died

hegeh19460819-01.2.12.note: Leon Clarmont, of the Or, transferred sick to the Atlit hospital, died on Friday evening; his funeral left the Government Hospital at 2 p.m.; "only known that he was about 40, and according to the Government Hospital's announcement he died of pneumonia."

hegeh19460823-01.2.19.note: - 1946-08-23 (hegeh19460823-01.2.19, hmf19460823-01.2.86, hzh19460823-01.2.67) — Edith Reinitz (13) and Eleonora Levy (12), both Romanian, taken off the deportation ship Empire Heywood to the infectious-diseases department with scarlet fever; Sara Hamburger recovered and was discharged. The three papers give the girls' names three slightly different ways.

hegeh19470212-01.2.8.note:
"3 people were transferred to the Government Hospital and several sick people were taken to Atlit after being examined at the Government Hospital."

The Exodus, July 1947 (ahr19470720-01.2.11, hzh19470720-01.2.2, hmf19470721-01.2.4) — 4,389 deportees, 955 of them children; 28 sick and 34 of their relatives left in the country. "The sick sent to the Government Hospital are 17 men, 10 women and one child," with 34 relatives as escorts; 22 of them were then sent on to Atlit. Named among those who stayed: Aryeh Birenbaum (26), serious; William Milman (24), broken jaw; Ernst Weiss (24), chest wound on the left; Moshe Engelman. The dead: Zvi Yakubovitz (15), born in Bendin, Poland, of the Hancha children's kibbutz, whose brother had come before him and was in Atlit; Mordechai Baumstein (23); and a third who died in the hospital. "The dead were brought to the hospital half-naked." A woman died in childbirth — reportedly Pola Abramovitch — and her body was buried at sea. Of the wounded taken to the hospital, all were later moved to Atlit; six sick remained, "among them a girl of two ill with chickenpox, and her mother is with her."

On 21 July "three new graves were dug in the row of the martyrs of the ha'apala in the Haifa cemetery." At four in the afternoon a great crowd gathered beside the Government Hospital; the three bodies were brought out of the mortuary wrapped in blue-and-white flags and driven to the cemetery, Rabbi Dr Israel Goldstein eulogising.

Two men buried as "Abraham son of Abraham." On 11 February 1947 (dav19470212-01.2.6, hegeh19470212-01.2.8) the unknown ma'apil of the Lanegev, who died of wounds from the naval boarding, was buried from the Government Hospital in Bat Galim under that name — "the holy one who fell for the sanctification of the Name and of the Land." Nothing in his clothes identified him; his pockets held a comb in a leather case, a cigarette case and an empty notebook with a few unclear words. Minutes before the funeral a driver arrived saying he thought the dead man was his brother-in-law: Harry Laufer, born in Leipzig, a teacher of English, whose wife Barbara Seligman-Laufer had been deported to Cyprus with the rest. And in December 1946 (haretz19461206-01.2.74) the inquest on two Knesset Yisrael immigrants — Isaac Rosenbaum and an unknown "buried under the name Abraham son of Abraham" — heard "the testimony of the physician of the Government Hospital, who examined the bodies of the dead and performed autopsies on them," and found both died of army bullets, one to the head, one to the lungs and heart.

Anyone reading unnamed entries in the 1946–47 ledgers should know that this formula existed and what it covered.

hmf19390227-01.2.2.note: a bomb thrown into a Jewish lorry near the eastern railway station; the driver Yosef Mizrahi (23, native-born, wife and two children) and his assistant Reuven Kaplan (24, from Lithuania, eight years in the country, wife and daughter) killed outright. "Their bodies were taken to the Government Hospital and from there to Hadassah." The hospital receives the dead of both communities and releases them onward.

hmf19390423-01.2.36.note: "A foundling. On Friday night a child of three months was found beside the Government Hospital. Its identity has not yet been established." Four lines, and a whole category of admission.

hmf19400115-01.2.41.note: Haifa municipal budget debate: "in Haifa there is a community hospital, and there is also a government hospital whose building cost a great deal and whose upkeep too demands much." The municipality is arguing with the Government over a hospital that is district, not municipal.

hmf19401205-01.2.9.note:
1940-09-20 — the heavy raid. (hbkr19400922-01.2.39, hashaah19400923-01.2.15) The tin roof of a café collapsed on those inside. hmf19480126-01.2.34.note:
the fullest account, and it prints the findings of the special commission the Haifa Situation Committee appointed. Headline: "The Government Hospital in Haifa has become a purely Arab institution. The Jews left it because gang members took control of it."

The trigger: families of the Jewish patients demanded insistently that they be moved, and the parents of the pupils of the hospital's nursing school feared for their daughters' lives. "As a result, on 31.12.47 all the Jewish patients were transferred out of the Government Hospital, and the medical personnel left their work."

The commission's findings, which are the closest thing this corpus offers to an inspection of the wards:

- Many employees, "especially of the lower grades, appeared at the hospital armed with firearms; most also carry knives." - Threats against the nurses and trainees by low-grade employees and by "the Arab policemen stationed there to guard the prisoners." - "The wounded brought to the hospital are accompanied by their relatives and friends, or by armed gang members, and often a wounded man has armed bodyguards standing beside him day and night. These things were done openly and unhindered." - "In one case two shots were fired inside one of the hospital's lavatories." - "In one case an Arab prisoner was brought to the hospital and was spirited out of it." - "The hospital is enclosed by a stone wall about a metre and a half high," which does not answer. - "Near the turning on the Bat Galim road towards the hospital the Arab Legion is encamped. There were cases in which Arab Legion sentries threatened Jewish nurses and their escorts at gunpoint as they passed, chiefly in the evening — the threat reaching the point of loading a round into the barrel." - "Armed Arabs move about in large groups in the vicinity of the hospital and inside its courtyards, and they penetrate even into the patients' rooms. In one case several armed Arabs stopped a nurse and pointed a pistol at her; only when it became clear to them that this nurse was an Arab did they let her go."

And the settlement that failed: after weeks of negotiation "the mountain gave birth to a mouse" — two gates left open, one British and one Arab policeman at each, six more British policemen inside; no Jewish guard. The Yishuv institutions judged it insufficient.

The single most consequential sentence for this project sits in that same article, as an aside: "Incidentally: this hospital contains the only department for infectious diseases in the north of the country, and that is also the only department the Jewish population used." The Yishuv asked the Government to open an infectious-diseases department inside a Jewish settlement, offering to provide the premises if the Government supplied equipment and staff. No answer was received.

Two things follow. It sharpens the question of Haifa's lazaret further — for the whole north there was no separate infectious-diseases institution, this was it. And it bears on the confessional composition of the register: Jewish use of the Government Hospital was, on the Yishuv's own account, largely confined to one department.

That is the point of it: it establishes from outside that the hospital was admitting patients and its deaths were being reported — which means the missing notebooks are missing, not never-written. The register confirms it to the month: Jewish admissions run at 20, 59, 12, 26 and 35 a month through 1947, then 1 in January 1948, 2 in February, 0 in March, 0 in April. The Hebrew dailies supply the date and the cause — the walkout of 31 December 1947 (§09).

wdt19260415.note: The Borromean Sisters' hospital tells its own history in the Templer weekly: the sisters took over a pilgrim house in 1888 and ran a poor-dispensary; in 1898 they rented a neighbouring house that had served the Templer community as schoolhouse and prayer hall, later buying and enlarging it when the Hejaz railway brought sick European labourers. Dr Peters directed it to 1913, then Dr Wilhelm Hoffmann, a grandson of the Templer colony's founder. Admissions rose from 155 in 1899 to 760 in 1925. It served the German communities of Haifa, Waldheim and Bethlehem of Galilee first, but was “fast immer überfüllt.”

ytlv19390115-01.2.10.note: A retrospective notice of the December opening, repeating the costs and the five-part plan, and adding a line the December reports do not: "The hospital is open to all communities."

ytlv19440416-01.2.11.note:
In a Tel Aviv municipal debate: "with the appointment of Dr Mc-Cowen as director of the Government Department of Health, in place of Colonel Heron, we hope for a change for the better."

This resolves two earlier readings at once. The man who left the directorship of the Haifa Government Hospital in November 1939 to become deputy director of the Department of Health (hzh19391123-01.2.46, OCR מק־טווין) is the same Dr McCowen who became its director in 1944 — Haifa was a step on that ladder. And Colonel Heron is the "Director of Government Medical Services" who read out Mendelsohn's letter of apology at the December 1938 opening; the phrase לקול הארון in the Davar report of the ceremony is "to Colonel Heron", not, as I first read it, a consul. The correction is recorded here rather than silently made above.
